The crop shows four strokes converging on one point in a star: the two ladder wires arrive from upper-left and lower-left, the 10ohm resistor lead leaves straight down, and the rail to the 2A source leaves to the right. No stroke passes through; every branch terminates. The 'hop=5.7' metric is just the curvature of the incoming ladder wire, not a jog. A crossing reading here would strand the 10ohm resistor top and the 2A source top on separate nets from the inductors, which the drawing plainly contradicts.
  S7 (208,403) deg4 -> JUNCTION (OVERRIDES the tracer default of 'crossing'). Verified in the pixel dump (inkmap 208 403 20): the horizontal wire from the left rail ENDS at x~210 (nothing horizontal continues to the right of the meeting point); from that same point three strokes radiate - a ~45-deg diagonal up-right to L#2, a ~35-deg diagonal down-right to L#5, and a vertical down the 3ohm resistor. Four terminating branches, no through-line, no dot needed, no hop or jog. The crossing reading the tracer chose would have paired the left rail with the down-right diagonal and split this into two nets - putting the 1A source top and L#2 on one net and L#5 + the 3ohm top on another - which contradicts the star geometry in the ink.

All one node. A crossing reading at either would leave the 10V source or the 20ohm resistor with no return path.

The crop shows a clean 4-way star: 3ohm resistor down from above, the left rail to the 1A source going left, the wire to V-DC #10 going up-right, and the 20ohm branch going down-right. Every branch terminates at the point. Crossing would strand the 10V source's left terminal.
